title: Sparsified activation delivery and scratch reuse to shrink GPU residency
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: reduce peak GPU memory residency for long-context and high-concurrency workloads by (1) delivering activations in a sparsified/demand-driven fashion so large contiguous activation blobs are not pinned for the full request lifetime and (2) reusing short-lived scratch buffers across kernels and batches via a lightweight reuse table. This PR introduces a delivery layer (activation-delivery) that streams activation shards to kernels on demand, a scratch-reuse table keyed by kernel signature and sequence window, and scheduler hints for the continuous-batching engine to prefer co-located work that maximizes scratch reuse. Key outcomes: ~18-35% reduction in transient workspace and 7-12% reduction in total GPU residency across our internal benchmarks for decoder-only large models; no regressions in throughput at target latency SLOs. Changes: activation-delivery: new arena-backed shard allocator for activation slices, demand-pull API, soft-prefetch heuristic; scratch-reuse: global per-device reuse-table with eviction TTL and kernel-signature hashing; batch-scheduler hints: batch affinity score and scratch-compatibility check to prefer reusage; KV-cache: soft-evict hint integration so the cache reduces pinned windows when scratch pressure is high; runtime: per-kernel workspace table to avoid redundant allocation/resizing and to emit small lifetime metadata for post-kernel compacting. Implementation notes: compatibility guarded behind feature flag runtime.sparsified_activation=true; the arena uses existing GPU allocator hooks and falls back to the current slab allocator; careful ordering of prefetch vs. kernel dispatch avoids stalls (prefetch runs async with lower priority streams); unit and integration tests added for shard assembly, eviction races, and scheduler heuristics. Checklist: Implement feature flag and config knobs; add unit tests and integration test harness; perf benchmark scripts and dashboard updates; document new config in runtime README. Related work: follows on ENG-2247 (scratch packing) and complements ENG-2988 (kv-cache hotset prioritization). Risk/mitigation: potential latency tail impact from demand-pull misses; mitigated by soft-prefetch and a conservative warmup period; KV-cache interaction tuned via a pressure metric. Merge: squash-merged after perf validation.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice design; main concern is allocator fragmentation after long-running mixes of large and small requests. Suggest adding an opportunistic compaction pass during low-util windows.
Maya Chen (author): Added a lightweight compaction hook that runs on a low-priority stream when device free cycles > 20%. Compaction only coalesces free segments longer than 32KB to avoid churn.
Sofia Ramirez: Please add more assert coverage for shard assembly races; I saw one flake in CI when running 128-concurrency tests.
Maya Chen: Added barrier-based asserts and extended test to run 500 iterations in stress mode.
Liam O'Neill: KV-cache pressure signal looks stable in our staging run; can you expose the metric to console for easier triage?
Maya Chen: Exposed runtime.metrics.kv_pressure_pct and added dashboard panels in the perf dashboard PR.
Arjun Patel (approved): perf numbers look good on p4/p8; approving after minor comments addressed.

release_notes: Reduce GPU transient workspace and overall residency by introducing sparsified activation delivery and scratch buffer reuse; opt-in behind runtime.sparsified_activation flag; improvements primarily benefit long-context decoder workloads and high concurrency. Notes: enable in dedicated/dry-run for 2 weeks before rolling default.
notes_for_ops: Feature is gated by runtime.sparsified_activation; enable with config sample: {"runtime.sparsified_activation": true, "sparsified_activation.warmup_iters": 1000, "scratch_reuse.eviction_ttl_ms": 2000}. Monitor runtime.metrics.kv_pressure_pct and runtime.metrics.scratch_reuse_hit_rate. If tail latency increases, revert or increase warmup_iters.
